name: AECi — WAF rate-limit / challenge spike (15m)
message:
Cloudflare WAF mitigations (blocks + challenges) on the production app host exceeded the spike threshold over the last 15m (AECI-262 / §15.1). `aeci.waf.ratelimit.blocked` is emitted by the hourly WAF firewall-event poll (`apps/api/src/scheduled.ts` `runWafMetricsJob`, AECI-262), which reads the previous clock hour of the zone's `firewallEventsAdaptiveGroups` over Cloudflare's GraphQL Analytics API. The value is the event count, so query it with `sum:` + `.as_count()` (OBSERVABILITY gotcha 3); split by the `action` (block / managed_challenge), `rule`, `host`, and `source` (ratelimit / firewallcustom) tags to see what fired. A sustained spike usually means either a scripted flood tripping the rate-limit rules (Rule A `/api/requests/*`, Rule B `/api/reviews`) or a scraper run hitting the UA Managed-Challenge rule — cross-reference Cloudflare → Security → Events (filter by the same rule/action/host) for the offending IPs. Legitimate users never approach these thresholds; if a real user is being challenged, re-tune the rule in `docs/waf-rate-limits.md`.

Note: detection lags up to ~1h because the source is an hourly poll, and there is deliberately NO notify_no_data — a quiet hour emits nothing (no attacks = healthy), so a no-data alert would be constant noise. Cron-liveness is carried separately by the always-emitted `aeci.waf.poll{outcome:ok}` heartbeat. The >500/15m threshold is a launch-tunable starting point — set it once production traffic + baseline mitigation volume are known.

Runbook: https://github.com/the-wbs-project/aec-integrations/blob/main/docs/RUNBOOKS.md#waf-rate-limit--challenge-spike
